title: Testing Directives and Pipes knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Testing Directives and Pipes”?
options: Testing Directives and Pipes helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Testing Directives and Pipes means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Testing Directives and Pipes removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Testing Directives and Pipes should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Testing Directives and Pipes helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Testing Directives and Pipes is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Testing DOM behavior” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Testing DOM behavior” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Testing DOM behavior” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Testing DOM behavior” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Testing DOM behavior” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Testing DOM behavior” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Testing DOM behavior” under Testing Directives and Pipes. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Testing Directives and Pipes”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
